description: Audit given Kotlin class(es)/file(s)/package scope in a JVM Kotlin project (plain library, Kotlin Spring Boot, or Kotlin Quarkus — not Android, which `iru-android-dokka` covers) for complete KDoc coverage — type-level docs, primary-constructor parameters (`@property` for declared properties, `@param` for plain parameters, `@constructor` where construction has its own behavior), every function and property within the discovered visibility bar (including Spring beans' and Quarkus CDI beans' public methods, `@ConfigurationProperties`/`@ConfigMapping` properties, and data classes' properties), enum entries, companion-object members, top-level and nested declarations — required tags `@param`/`@return`/`@throws`/`@see`/`@sample`, `@suppress` honored, and Dokka module/package includes (`module.md` with `# Module`/`# Package` sections) wired for every module/package touched (creating them if missing) — generate any missing or incomplete KDoc grounded in the actual code and current changes, then run the project's Dokka build to confirm the KDoc is well-formed: Gradle `org.jetbrains.dokka` (Dokka 2 `dokkaGenerate`/`dokkaGeneratePublicationHtml`, or Dokka 1 `dokkaHtml`, wrapper preferred, Kotlin DSL or Groovy) or Maven `org.jetbrains.dokka:dokka-maven-plugin` (`dokka:dokka`). Invoke as `/iru-kotlin-kdoc <scope>` where `<scope>` is a comma-separated list of class names, file paths, or a package glob, or `/iru-kotlin-kdoc` with no argument to scope to Kotlin files touched by uncommitted changes plus commits on the current branch not yet on the base branch. Discovers the project's own documentation bar (detekt `comments` rules, Dokka `documentedVisibilities`/`reportUndocumented`, contributor guides, observed practice) rather than assuming a fixed style. Use whenever the user wants KDoc completeness checked and filled in for specific Kotlin classes/modules, instead of relying on a Dokka run to surface gaps (Dokka does not fail on undocumented members by default).
